info.name: Tandil Backend - Flow-Based Collection
info.description:
Tandil Backend API. All responses JSON. Set env: base_url, token. Use Bearer token for protected routes.

Organized by dashboard: ADMIN DASHBOARD (Banners, Packages, Orders Export, Stats & HR, Reports, Settings) · CLIENT DASHBOARD (Profile, Memberships, Addresses, Payment Methods, Notifications as Tips, Help Center, Shop & Orders, Maintenance Photos) · TECHNICIAN DASHBOARD (folder 9, technician only) · SUPERVISOR DASHBOARD (folder 10, supervisor only). Support APIs remain under client/help-support sections.

item.name: 4. Client Dashboard – Subscriptions

request.description: ✅ STEP 4: Get available subscription plans (Public - no auth needed)

✅ STEP 5: Create a new subscription (visits will be auto-generated)

**Required Fields:**
- `plan` (string): Subscription plan - one of: `1_month`, `3_month`, `6_month`, `12_month`

**Optional Fields:**
- `start_date` (date): Start date of subscription (defaults to today)
- `end_date` (date): End date of subscription (auto-calculated if not provided)
- `amount` (decimal): Subscription amount in AED (auto-calculated from plan if not provided)
- `payment_status` (string): Payment status - one of: `pending`, `paid`, `failed`, `refunded`, `cancelled` (defaults to `pending`)
- `payment_reference` (string): Payment reference number (optional)
- `client_id` (integer): Client user ID (only admins can set this, defaults to authenticated user)
- `total_visits` (integer): Total number of visits (defaults to plan months)
- `completed_visits` (integer): Number of completed visits (defaults to 0)

**Note:** If `payment_status` is `paid` and `paid_at` is not provided, it will be automatically set to current timestamp.

✅ STEP 6: List all subscriptions (client sees own, admin sees all)

**Returns:**
- Array of subscriptions
- Clients see only their own subscriptions
- Admins see all subscriptions
- Includes subscription details and client info

**Use Cases:**
- Subscription management dashboard
- Client subscription history
- Admin overview of all subscriptions

✅ STEP 7: Get subscription details with visits

**Returns:**
- Full subscription information
- Associated visits with status
- Client information (if admin)
- Payment details and dates

**Use Cases:**
- View subscription details page
- Check visit schedule
- Review payment status

Mark subscription as paid

**Purpose:**
- Updates subscription payment_status to 'paid'
- Sends notification to client about payment confirmation
- Can be used by admin or subscription owner

**Use Cases:**
- After payment gateway webhook confirmation
- Manual payment confirmation by admin
- Client confirming their own payment

Update subscription details

**Updatable Fields (Admin Only):**
- `amount` (decimal): Update subscription price/amount in AED
- `payment_status` (string): Update payment status - one of: `pending`, `paid`, `failed`, `refunded`, `cancelled`
- `total_visits` (integer): Update total number of visits
- `completed_visits` (integer): Update number of completed visits
- `payment_reference` (string): Payment transaction ID or reference

**Updatable Fields (All Users):**
- `start_date` (date): Update subscription start date
- `end_date` (date): Update subscription end date

**Note:** Only admins can update `amount`, `payment_status`, `total_visits`, `completed_visits`, and `payment_reference`. Regular users can only update dates for their own subscriptions.

Cancel/delete subscription

**Purpose:**
- Permanently deletes a subscription
- Can be used by admin or subscription owner
- All associated visits will be deleted (cascade)

**Use Cases:**
- Client cancelling their subscription
- Admin removing invalid subscriptions
- Refund processing

item.description: Subscription management - Get plans, create, view, update subscriptions

request.description:
Get all active banners for customer home screen / app slider.

**Purpose:**
- Returns all active banners ordered by priority (lower = first)
- Public endpoint - no authentication required

**Response (each item):**

**Use Cases:**

item.name: 8. Client Dashboard – Shop & Orders

request.description: GET /api/shop/settings – Shop settings for client (shipping_amount, tax_percent, currency). No auth. Use in cart/checkout UI.
PUT /api/shop/settings – Client can update shop settings (shipping_amount, tax_percent). Auth: Bearer token with client role. Same as admin PUT.

GET /api/shop/order-summary – Order summary for checkout (Address/Payment/Review). Auth: Bearer token (client).

**Tax-exclusive:** Subtotal = sum of cart item prices (no tax). Total = Subtotal − discount + shipping + (Subtotal × tax_percent/100). Response returns tax_percent only (no tax amount).

**Response (data):**
- subtotal (number) – Sum of items before tax
- discount (number) – Currently 0
- shipping (number) – From settings (0 = free)
- shipping_label (string) – "Free" or amount for display
- tax_percent (number) – e.g. 5 for 5%
- total (number) – Grand total
- currency (string) – e.g. "AED"
✅ STEP 14: Add product to cart

GET /api/shop/cart – Shopping Cart screen. Response: items (id, product_id, name, image_url, category, brand, current_price, original_price, quantity, line_total, currency), order_summary (subtotal, discount, shipping, shipping_label [Free or amount], tax_percent, tax, total, currency). Admin can set shipping and tax via PUT /api/admin/settings/shop.
PUT /api/shop/cart/:id – Update quantity (Shopping Cart +/-). Body: { "quantity": number }. Set cart_item_id. Response: updated item (same shape as cart view).
DELETE /api/shop/cart/:id – Remove item (trash icon). Set cart_item_id.

GET /api/shop/checkout/payment-methods – Checkout Payment step. Response: array of { id, type, label } for card, apple_pay, samsung_pay, tabby, tamara (all via Checkout.com). Use POST /create-payment-session next.

POST /api/shop/create-payment-session – Backend creates order (pending) and Checkout.com session. Body: address_id (or full_name, phone_number, street_address, city, country), optional items (omit to use cart), success_url (required), failure_url (required). Returns: session_id, order_id, order_number, public_key, amount, currency. Frontend opens Checkout.com UI with session_id; webhook updates order to paid.

Guest: no Authorization. Required: email, full_name, phone_number, street_address, city, country, items (array of {product_id, qty}), success_url, failure_url. Returns session_id, order_id, order_number, public_key. Use order_number + email for guest lookup/track.

GET /api/shop/checkout/review – Checkout Review step. Response: items (cart), order_summary, addresses, payment_methods (card, apple_pay, samsung_pay, tabby, tamara). Then call POST /create-payment-session with success_url and failure_url.
Legacy endpoint. Returns 400: use POST /api/shop/create-payment-session for payment. PayPal and COD removed.

item.name: 11. Admin Dashboard – Stats, Users & HR

request.description:
Get admin dashboard statistics for mobile app

**Purpose:**
- Returns comprehensive statistics for total users, active subscriptions, monthly revenue, customers, technicians, and employees
- Includes counts/amounts for daily, weekly, monthly, yearly periods
- Provides growth percentages vs previous periods with automatic + and - signs
- Used by admin mobile app dashboard

**Response Structure:**
- `total_users`: All users regardless of role (total, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly + growth)
- `active_subscriptions`: Paid subscriptions that haven't expired (total, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly + growth)
- `monthly_revenue`: Total revenue from orders + subscriptions (total, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly + growth)
- `customers`: Total count + daily/weekly/monthly/yearly counts + growth percentages
- `technicians`: Total count + daily/weekly/monthly/yearly counts + growth percentages
- `employees`: Total count (Technicians + Supervisors + Area Managers + HR) + daily/weekly/monthly/yearly counts + growth percentages

**Growth Format:**
- Growth values are strings with automatic + or - sign (e.g., "+12", "+8", "+15", "-5")
- Positive growth: Always includes '+' sign (e.g., "+12", "+8", "+15")
- Negative growth: Always includes '-' sign (e.g., "-5", "-10")
- Zero growth: Shows as "+0" or "0"
- Represents percentage change vs previous period
- No need to add + or - sign in frontend, it's already included

**Use Cases:**
- Admin mobile app dashboard
- Display statistics cards (Total Users, Active Subscriptions, Monthly Revenue, Total Employees)
- Show growth trends with visual indicators (green for +, red for -)
- Analytics overview

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "total_users": {
      "total": 1245,
      "daily": 5,
      "weekly": 25,
      "monthly": 120,
      "yearly": 1245,
      "growth": {
        "daily": "+2",
        "weekly": "+15",
        "monthly": "+12",
        "yearly": "+200"
      }
    },
    "active_subscriptions": {
      "total": 892,
      "daily": 3,
      "weekly": 15,
      "monthly": 60,
      "yearly": 892,
      "growth": {
        "daily": "+1",
        "weekly": "+8",
        "monthly": "+8",
        "yearly": "+150"
      }
    },
    "monthly_revenue": {
      "total": 245000,
```

Get recent activities for React Native dashboard

**Purpose:**
- Returns a list of recent activities including subscriptions, customer registrations, inventory alerts, and orders (real data only; no visit data)
- Used to display the "Recent Activities" section in admin mobile app

**Activity Types:**
- `subscription`: New paid subscriptions (icon_type: success - green checkmark)
- `customer`: New customer registrations (icon_type: user_add - user icon with plus sign)
- `inventory`: Low stock or out of stock alerts (icon_type: warning/error - yellow/red icon)
- `order`: New orders placed (icon_type: order - shopping cart icon)

**Response Structure:**
Each activity contains:
- `type`: Activity type (subscription, customer, inventory, order)
- `icon_type`: Icon type for frontend rendering (success, user_add, warning, error, order)
- `description`: Human-readable activity description
- `timestamp`: Human-readable time (e.g., "5 min ago", "1 hour ago")
- `created_at`: ISO 8601 timestamp for sorting
- `related_id`: ID of related entity
- `related_type`: Type of related entity (subscription, user, product, order)
- Additional fields for specific types (e.g., `stock` for inventory, `amount` and `status` for orders)

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "type": "subscription",
      "icon_type": "success",
      "description": "New 12-month subscription by Palm Grove Estate",
      "timestamp": "5 min ago",
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "related_id": 123,
      "related_type": "subscription"
    },
    {
      "type": "customer",
      "icon_type": "user_add",
      "description": "New customer registered - Mohammed Ali Farm",
      "timestamp": "1 hour ago",
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T09:30:00Z",
      "related_id": 456,
      "related_type": "user"
    },
    {
      "type": "inventory",
      "icon_type": "warning",
      "description": "Low inventory alert: Organic Fertilizer",
      "timestamp": "2 hours ago",
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T08:30:00Z",
      "related_id": 789,
      "related_type": "product",
      "stock": 5
    },
    {
      "type": "order",
      "icon_type": "order",
      "description": "New order #101 by John Doe",
      "timestamp": "3 hours ago",
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T07:30:00Z",
      "related_id": 101,
      "related_type": "order",
      "amount": 150.50,
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ],
  "total": 4
}
```

**Use Cases:**
- Display recent activities in admin mobile app dashboard
- Show activity feed with icons and timestamps
- Navigate to related entities using `related_id` and `related_type`
- Filter or group activities by type

**Query Parameters:**
- `limit` (optional): Number of activities to return (default: 20, max recommended: 50)

**Frontend Implementation:**
- Use `icon_type` to render appropriate icons (success=green checkmark, user_add=user icon with plus, warning=yellow alert, error=red alert, order=shopping cart)
- Display `description` as main text
- Show `timestamp` as secondary text (e.g., "5 min ago")
- Use `related_id` and `related_type` for navigation when user taps on activity

Get quick overview statistics for React Native dashboard

**Purpose:**
- Returns quick stats for dashboard cards including pending reports, new orders, support tickets, new customers, etc.
- Includes percentage growth vs previous period (yesterday)
- Used to display "Quick Overview" cards in admin mobile app

**Response Structure:**
- `pending_reports`: Count of reports with status 'pending' + growth percentage
- `new_orders`: Count of orders created today + growth percentage
- `support_tickets`: Count of open/in_progress complaints + growth percentage
- `new_customers`: Count of customers registered today + growth percentage
- `new_subscriptions`: Count of paid subscriptions created today + growth percentage
- `revenue_today`: Total revenue from paid orders today + growth percentage
- `pending_visits`: Count of scheduled but not completed visits + growth percentage

**Growth Format:**
- Growth values are strings with automatic + or - sign (e.g., "+12", "-5")
- Positive growth: Includes '+' sign (e.g., "+12", "+8")
- Negative growth: Includes '-' sign (e.g., "-5", "-10")
- Zero growth: Shows as "0" or "+0"
- Represents percentage change vs previous period (yesterday)

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "pending_reports": {
      "count": 12,
      "growth": "+20",
      "label": "Pending Reports"
    },
    "new_orders": {
      "count": 34,
      "growth": "+12",
      "label": "New Orders"
    },
    "support_tickets": {
      "count": 8,
      "growth": "-5",
      "label": "Support Tickets"
    },
    "new_customers": {
      "count": 5,
      "growth": "+25",
      "label": "New Customers"
    },
    "new_subscriptions": {
      "count": 3,
      "growth": "+50",
      "label": "New Subscriptions"
    },
    "revenue_today": {
      "amount": 12500.50,
      "growth": "+15",
      "label": "Revenue Today"
    },
    "pending_visits": {
      "count": 12,
      "growth": "-8",
      "label": "Pending Visits"
    }
  }
}
```

**Use Cases:**
- Display quick overview cards in admin mobile app dashboard
- Show counts with growth indicators (green for +, red for -)
- Quick access to key metrics
- Display "New" badge for items with new activity

**Frontend Implementation:**
- Display `count` or `amount` as main number
- Show `growth` with appropriate color (green for +, red for -)
- Use `label` for card title
- Display growth with arrow icons (up for +, down for -)
- Show "New" badge for items with positive growth or new items

Get admin user profile with formatted ID for React Native dashboard

**Purpose:**
- Returns current admin user's profile information
- Includes formatted ID (e.g., "ADMIN-5001") for display
- Includes time-based greeting (Good morning/afternoon/evening/night)
- Used to display user info at top of admin mobile app dashboard

**Response Structure:**
- `id`: User ID
- `formatted_id`: Formatted ID with role prefix (e.g., "ADMIN-5001")
- `name`: User's full name
- `email`: User's email
- `phone`: User's phone number
- `role`: User's role (admin, supervisor, etc.)
- `role_display_name`: Human-readable role name (e.g., "Executive Management")
- `status`: User status (active, inactive, etc.)
- `greeting`: Time-based greeting (Good morning/afternoon/evening/night)
- `avatar`: Avatar URL (null if not set)
- `created_at`: Account creation timestamp

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 5001,
    "formatted_id": "ADMIN-5001",
    "name": "Abdullah Al Mazrouei",
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "phone": "+971501234567",
    "role": "admin",

    "status": "active",
    "greeting": "Good afternoon!",
    "avatar": null,

  }
}
```

**Use Cases:**
- Display user profile section at top of admin mobile app dashboard
- Show greeting, name, role, and formatted ID
- Display user avatar if available

**Frontend Implementation:**
- Display `greeting` as greeting text
- Show `name` as main heading
- Display `role_display_name` as subtitle
- Show `formatted_id` as ID label (e.g., "ID: ADMIN-5001")
